title: Group ISMS scope with property baselines
objective: Direct and oversee information security in the same way across every property under one accountable structure.
requirement: [GROUP] shall define one information security management system scope that names every property with its systems and operating model. Each property shall adopt the group baseline with any local variation recorded and approved.
rationale: Properties run separate directories and uneven builds, so a single scope with property baselines is needed before any control can be checked consistently (E04, E10).
evidence_expected: ISMS scope statement listing every property;signed property baseline adoption record
assessment_question: Does a current ISMS scope name every property and does each property hold an approved baseline adoption record?

title: Named security owner per property
objective: Direct and oversee information security in the same way across every property under one accountable structure.
requirement: Each property shall have a named information security owner with a deputy who covers night and weekend shifts. Group security roles shall be recorded with their authority over property decisions.
rationale: Hotels never close, so a single daytime contact leaves incidents without a decision maker at night (E17).
evidence_expected: role assignment record or RACI for each property;contact roster covering every shift
assessment_question: Can the property show a named security owner and deputy whose cover includes nights and weekends?

title: Hotel policy set
objective: Direct and oversee information security in the same way across every property under one accountable structure.
requirement: [GROUP] shall maintain an approved policy set written for hotel roles that covers at least acceptable use, access, vendor access, guest data, payment data, incident response and backup, reviewed every year and after any major incident.
rationale: No policies were found in the case files (E20); generic templates do not speak to front desk, engineering or vendor realities.
evidence_expected: approved policy index with review record;property acknowledgement of the current policy set
assessment_question: Is there an approved hotel policy set covering the listed topics with a review in the last twelve months?

title: Control applicability record
objective: Direct and oversee information security in the same way across every property under one accountable structure.
requirement: Each property shall keep an applicability record that states for every HISS control whether it applies, the reason and the accountable party under the operating model, refreshed whenever the profile or triggers change.
rationale: The group ISO and SOC 2 sheets carry no status or evidence columns (E15), so nothing shows which controls each property actually owns.
evidence_expected: applicability record generated by HISS-Assess;approval sign off by the property owner
assessment_question: Does each property hold a current applicability record that names an accountable party per control?

title: Exception and operational override register
objective: Direct and oversee information security in the same way across every property under one accountable structure.
requirement: Any departure from a HISS control made to keep guest service running, such as a shared front desk logon during an outage or a vendor session opened without approval, shall be entered in an exception register with the reason, approving manager, compensating measure and expiry. The register shall be reviewed monthly.
rationale: Operations teams override IT rules to protect the guest experience (E17); recording overrides turns silent drift into a managed risk.
evidence_expected: exception register with expiry dates;monthly review minutes
assessment_question: Are all current overrides of security rules logged with an approver and an expiry and reviewed in the last month?

title: Asset and software inventory including engineering assets
objective: Know the assets, risks and legal duties of each property and measure progress against them.
requirement: Each property shall keep an inventory of hardware, software, cloud services and engineering assets with owner, location, network zone, support end date and criticality tier, reconciled with discovery scans at least quarterly.
rationale: Software seen in the scans (E10) and the assumed engineering estate (A13) were not listed anywhere, so unsupported systems stayed invisible.
evidence_expected: inventory export with tiers and support dates;quarterly reconciliation against discovery scans
assessment_question: Does the inventory include engineering assets and support end dates and was it reconciled with a scan this quarter?

title: Property risk assessment cycle
objective: Know the assets, risks and legal duties of each property and measure progress against them.
requirement: [GROUP] shall assess risk for each property at least yearly and after major change, using scan findings, asset tiers and hotel impact scenarios through HISS-RAT or an equivalent method. Treatment decisions shall be recorded with owners.
rationale: The case risk matrix lists ten generic risks, all open and unscored (E14).
evidence_expected: scored risk register per property;treatment plan with owners and dates
assessment_question: Was each property risk assessed in the last twelve months with treatment owners recorded?

title: Obligations register per jurisdiction
objective: Know the assets, risks and legal duties of each property and measure progress against them.
requirement: [GROUP] shall keep a register of legal, regulatory and contractual security and privacy duties for each jurisdiction where it has properties or guests, giving the hotel trigger, deadline and owner of each, reviewed on entry to any new jurisdiction.
rationale: Hotels face guest registers, card data rules and breach clocks that differ by country and emirate; the case group relied on the IT Act and CERT-In directions as its baseline (A17).
evidence_expected: obligations register with owners;record of legal review
assessment_question: Does the register list every applicable duty with a trigger, deadline and owner for each operating jurisdiction?

title: Annual HISS self assessment
objective: Know the assets, risks and legal duties of each property and measure progress against them.
requirement: Each property shall complete a HISS self assessment every year, scoring each applicable control on the 0 to 4 maturity scale with an evidence reference. The group shall verify a sample of that evidence.
rationale: The existing IT assessment template has ten generic sections and no hotel prompts (E16).
evidence_expected: completed self assessment file;group evidence verification record
assessment_question: Has the property completed a scored self assessment this year and has the group checked a sample of evidence?

title: Security metrics to owners
objective: Know the assets, risks and legal duties of each property and measure progress against them.
requirement: [GROUP] shall report a small set of security metrics per property to owners and management at least quarterly, including open critical findings, patch age, access review completion, backup restore results and open exceptions.
rationale: Owners and operators fund fixes they can see; the case risk matrix carried no measures (E14).
evidence_expected: quarterly metrics report per property;management review minutes
assessment_question: Did owners receive the agreed security metrics for every property last quarter?

title: First shift induction for all workers
objective: Make every person who uses hotel systems able and accountable to work securely from the first shift.
requirement: Every new, seasonal, agency or outsourced worker who will use a hotel system shall complete a short role based security induction covering logon rules, guest data, card handling and how to report a problem, recorded before credentials are issued.
rationale: System users are often not IT specialists (E17) and seasonal staff start on a live shift, so long courses arrive too late.
evidence_expected: signed induction checklist;training record linked to the account creation ticket
assessment_question: For a sample of recent joiners, was the induction recorded before their account was created?

title: Leaver removal within the shift
objective: Make every person who uses hotel systems able and accountable to work securely from the first shift.
requirement: Access for any worker who leaves, ends a seasonal contract or is withdrawn by an agency shall be disabled before the end of the shift in which the exit is recorded. Badges, key cards and devices shall be returned or disabled the same day.
rationale: High turnover and shared terminals mean an active leaver account can be used by anyone who knows it.
evidence_expected: leaver checklist with timestamps;comparison of account disable times against HR exit records
assessment_question: For a sample of leavers, was access disabled within the shift of the recorded exit?

title: Front desk social engineering awareness
objective: Make every person who uses hotel systems able and accountable to work securely from the first shift.
requirement: Front desk, reservations and call centre staff shall be trained at least twice a year to verify callers and visitors before sharing guest details, issuing duplicate key cards or changing bookings, using scripted checks that also work at night and at peak times.
rationale: Pretext calls and duplicate key requests target the front desk because it must be helpful at all hours.
evidence_expected: training attendance record;results of test calls or visitor checks
assessment_question: Have front desk and reservations staff been trained in the last six months and tested with a scripted check?

title: Shared terminal rules
objective: Make every person who uses hotel systems able and accountable to work securely from the first shift.
requirement: Shared terminals at the front desk, outlets, back office and engineering shall lock after a short idle period, show no guest data on the lock screen and block personal browsing, unscanned removable media and local storage of guest documents.
rationale: Shared front office folders and USB media are assumed leakage points (A15) and SMB weaknesses make shared folders easier to reach (E06).
evidence_expected: group policy or device management configuration export;spot check record of terminals
assessment_question: Do sampled shared terminals lock when idle and block removable media and local guest documents?

title: Acceptable use for hotel roles
objective: Make every person who uses hotel systems able and accountable to work securely from the first shift.
requirement: All workers shall acknowledge an acceptable use statement written in plain language for hotel roles and available in the main local languages, before first use and after each yearly update.
rationale: Many hotel staff work in a language other than English and read rules on a shift break, not at a desk.
evidence_expected: signed acknowledgements;policy version record
assessment_question: Has every active user acknowledged the current acceptable use statement?

title: Individual logons on shared terminals
objective: Tie every action on hotel systems to an identified person holding only the access the role needs.
requirement: Every person using a shared terminal or the PMS shall log on with an individual account. Shared terminals shall support fast user switching or a badge tap so that individual logon does not slow check in.
rationale: Shared front desk logons are common because speed matters at check in; logon practice was not visible in mostly uncredentialed scans (E02, E20).
evidence_expected: PMS user list showing no generic accounts;terminal logon configuration screenshot
assessment_question: Are all PMS and terminal users individual and does the front desk use fast user switching or badge logon?

title: Privileged access
objective: Tie every action on hotel systems to an identified person holding only the access the role needs.
requirement: Administrator rights on servers, domain controllers, PMS, POS and network devices shall be held by named accounts separate from daily accounts, kept to a recorded minimum and reviewed monthly. Administrator use from front desk terminals shall be blocked.
rationale: Domain controllers host applications and one carried Zerologon (E12, E13), so a single stolen administrator logon reaches the whole property.
evidence_expected: privileged account list with owners;monthly privileged access review record
assessment_question: Are administrator accounts named, separate from daily accounts and reviewed in the last month?

title: MFA for remote, admin and cloud access
objective: Tie every action on hotel systems to an identified person holding only the access the role needs.
requirement: Multi factor authentication shall be required for all remote access, all administrator access and all access to cloud consoles and SaaS administration, with phishing resistant methods preferred for administrators.
rationale: RDP without network level authentication and multiple remote tools were found (E09); FTC findings against a hotel group named insufficient multi factor authentication (USE B8).
evidence_expected: MFA enforcement policy export;list of exempt accounts with exception references
assessment_question: Is MFA enforced for every remote, administrator and cloud administration account?

title: Quarterly access review per property
objective: Tie every action on hotel systems to an identified person holding only the access the role needs.
requirement: Each property shall review user and role assignments in the PMS, POS, back office and directory every quarter with department heads confirming each user. Unconfirmed accounts shall be removed within five working days.
rationale: Seasonal hiring and transfers between properties leave stale accounts that no one owns.
evidence_expected: signed access review record;account removal tickets
assessment_question: Was a signed access review completed this quarter and were unconfirmed accounts removed?

title: Service and interface accounts
objective: Tie every action on hotel systems to an identified person holding only the access the role needs.
requirement: Service and interface accounts used by PMS interfaces, backup jobs and integrations shall be listed with an owner, denied interactive logon where the platform allows, use long unique secrets held in a vault and be rotated when staff who know them leave.
rationale: The interface server links PMS, POS and locks (A11) and domain controllers share roles with applications (E12), so service account misuse spreads fast.
evidence_expected: service account register;vault rotation log
assessment_question: Is every service account listed with an owner and rotated after the last relevant leaver?

title: Role hardening baselines
objective: Keep hotel systems configured, patched and encrypted to a known baseline without breaking round the clock service.
requirement: Each server and workstation role shall follow a written hardening baseline that requires SMB signing and disables LLMNR, SMBv1, legacy simple services and cleartext management protocols, checked by configuration scan after each build or change.
rationale: SMB signing was not required on 19 of 22 SMB hosts and LLMNR was enabled on 16 systems (E06), with cleartext and legacy services on several more (E08).
evidence_expected: hardening baseline per role;configuration scan report
assessment_question: Does a configuration scan show the baseline settings in place on every server and workstation role?

title: Patch windows that fit round the clock operation
objective: Keep hotel systems configured, patched and encrypted to a known baseline without breaking round the clock service.
requirement: Security patches shall be applied within set windows by severity, with critical vulnerabilities fixed within 30 days at most and sooner on internet facing or Tier 1 systems, using agreed low occupancy windows, a tested rollback and a manual fallback briefing for the front desk.
rationale: QueueJumper stayed open on three Tier 1 systems (E06) because a PMS that never stops leaves no obvious maintenance window.
evidence_expected: patch compliance report by severity;change records showing the occupancy window used
assessment_question: Were all critical patches applied within 30 days and were changes made in agreed windows?

title: TLS, SSH and certificate management
objective: Keep hotel systems configured, patched and encrypted to a known baseline without breaking round the clock service.
requirement: All internal and external services shall use current TLS versions and strong ciphers with SSL, TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1, 3DES and RC4 disabled. SSH shall use strong algorithms and key logon. Certificates shall come from a managed source, be listed in an inventory and be renewed before expiry.
rationale: Untrusted certificates appeared on 15 systems, legacy TLS on 13 and SWEET32 on 12 (E06); cryptography families held 89 of the 191 findings.
evidence_expected: certificate inventory with expiry dates;TLS and SSH configuration scan report
assessment_question: Does a scan show no legacy protocol or weak cipher and is every certificate listed with a renewal date?

title: Credentialed scanning and yearly testing
objective: Keep hotel systems configured, patched and encrypted to a known baseline without breaking round the clock service.
requirement: Each property shall run credentialed vulnerability scans of all servers and workstations at least monthly and after major change, plus a yearly internal penetration test by a qualified tester, with findings fed into the risk register.
rationale: 22 of 29 case scans were uncredentialed so patch status could not be judged (E02). The one VAPT covered six hosts and had internal inconsistencies (E13).
evidence_expected: scan schedule with credentialed coverage figures;penetration test report with remediation tracker
assessment_question: Are monthly scans credentialed on all in scope systems and was a penetration test done this year?

title: Malware protection
objective: Keep hotel systems configured, patched and encrypted to a known baseline without breaking round the clock service.
requirement: Centrally managed malware protection with alerting shall run on every server and workstation that supports it, including PMS, POS back office and engineering workstations. Removable media shall be scanned on insertion.
rationale: No antivirus evidence existed in the case files (E20) and USB media is an assumed path into engineering and front office (A15, A14).
evidence_expected: console coverage report against the inventory;alert handling record
assessment_question: Does the malware console cover every eligible device in the inventory and are alerts handled?

title: Central logs kept for the longest legal need
objective: Detect, report and recover from incidents fast enough to meet legal clocks and keep guests served.
requirement: Security relevant logs from PMS, POS, directory, firewalls, remote access, guest Wi-Fi gateway and CCTV recorders shall be collected centrally with clocks synchronised to a trusted time source and kept for the longest retention any applicable obligation requires, at least 180 days for Indian properties.
rationale: No logging evidence existed (E20) while CERT-In directions require 180 days of logs and synchronised clocks (IU A8).
evidence_expected: log source list with retention settings;time synchronisation configuration evidence
assessment_question: Are logs from every listed source held centrally for at least the required period with synchronised clocks?

title: Security monitoring every day of the year
objective: Detect, report and recover from incidents fast enough to meet legal clocks and keep guests served.
requirement: [GROUP] or a contracted monitoring service shall review alerts from central logs and security tools every day of the year, with defined use cases for failed and out of hours logons, new administrator accounts, remote tool use and bulk data export.
rationale: Attacks on hotels often run at night or on holidays when IT is absent; regulators named weak monitoring in hotel breach cases (USE A13, B8).
evidence_expected: monitoring use case list;alert triage records covering weekends and holidays
assessment_question: Are alerts triaged every day, including weekends, against the defined use cases?

title: Incident response with a notification clock matrix
objective: Detect, report and recover from incidents fast enough to meet legal clocks and keep guests served.
requirement: An incident response plan shall set roles, an out of hours contact chain and a notification clock matrix for each jurisdiction (for example 6 hours to CERT-In for Indian properties and 72 hours to the supervisory authority under GDPR where feasible). The plan shall be exercised yearly with front office and engineering staff.
rationale: No tested incident response plan existed (A18) and legal clocks range from hours to weeks across jurisdictions (IU A8, USE A1, USE B2).
evidence_expected: incident response plan with clock matrix;exercise report from the last twelve months
assessment_question: Does the plan hold a clock matrix for every operating jurisdiction and was it exercised this year?

title: Backup with offline copy and restore tests
objective: Detect, report and recover from incidents fast enough to meet legal clocks and keep guests served.
requirement: PMS, POS back office, finance and directory data shall be backed up daily with at least one encrypted copy offline or immutable. A full PMS restore shall be tested at least every six months with the time recorded against the recovery target.
rationale: The risk matrix rates the missing disaster recovery plan High for likelihood and impact (E14) and backups are assumed to copy to an unencrypted peer share (A15).
evidence_expected: backup job report;restore test record with measured recovery time
assessment_question: Was a full PMS restore tested in the last six months and does an offline or immutable copy exist?

title: Manual front desk fallback
objective: Detect, report and recover from incidents fast enough to meet legal clocks and keep guests served.
requirement: Each property shall keep a tested manual fallback for check in, check out, key issue and charge posting during a PMS or network outage, with paper forms stored securely, a limit on what card data may be written down and a procedure to re enter and then destroy the records after recovery.
rationale: Front desks fall back to paper during outages (A03), which moves guest and card data into a less protected form.
evidence_expected: fallback kit checklist;drill record including destruction of paper records
assessment_question: Was the manual fallback drilled this year and were the paper records destroyed after re entry?

title: Role based PMS access
objective: Protect the PMS and reservation data as the core record of every guest stay.
requirement: PMS roles shall be defined per job (such as front desk, night audit, reservations, revenue, housekeeping and finance) with screen level rights so that each role sees only the guest fields it needs. Rights to export, discount and void shall be limited to named supervisors.
rationale: The PMS is the core guest record (E10) and role based access is a named security characteristic of the NIST hotel PMS design (INT C5).
evidence_expected: PMS role matrix;user to role report
assessment_question: Does the PMS role matrix limit guest fields by job and restrict export, discount and void rights?

title: Tokens not card numbers in the PMS
objective: Protect the PMS and reservation data as the core record of every guest stay.
requirement: The PMS shall store only payment tokens or truncated card numbers and never full card numbers or security codes. Any card data found in PMS notes, profiles or attachments shall be purged.
rationale: Only tokens move through the PMS in the NIST design (INT C5) and Indian merchants may not keep card on file data (IU A13).
evidence_expected: PMS payment configuration showing tokenisation;data discovery scan of the PMS database and notes
assessment_question: Does a discovery scan of the PMS find no full card numbers in any field, note or attachment?

title: Interface server in a protected zone
objective: Protect the PMS and reservation data as the core record of every guest stay.
requirement: The PMS interface server that links POS, locks, telephony, in room systems and the channel manager shall sit in a protected zone, accept connections only from listed systems, run no other roles and be patched in the Tier 1 window.
rationale: The interface server carried legacy simple services (E08) and its failure breaks billing and key issue (A03, A11).
evidence_expected: firewall rule set for the protected zone;interface server role inventory
assessment_question: Is the interface server in a protected zone with listed sources only and no other roles?

title: PMS vendor patch and support status
objective: Protect the PMS and reservation data as the core record of every guest stay.
requirement: Each property shall record the PMS version, the vendor support end date and the vendor route for security notices. It shall plan an upgrade or migration at least 12 months before support ends.
rationale: Unsupported software was one of the twelve finding families in the case (E43) and PMS replacement takes longer than a patch cycle.
evidence_expected: PMS version and support record;vendor security notice subscription record
assessment_question: Is the PMS on a supported version with a known support end date and a plan if it ends within a year?

title: Reservation data export control
objective: Protect the PMS and reservation data as the core record of every guest stay.
requirement: Bulk exports of guest or reservation data from the PMS and CRM shall be limited to named roles, logged and sent only through approved encrypted channels, never as plain email attachments or to personal storage.
rationale: Emailed guest lists are an assumed leakage point at booking and CRM stages (A15).
evidence_expected: PMS export log;mail or data loss prevention rule report
assessment_question: Are bulk guest exports logged and blocked from plain email and personal storage?

title: Cardholder data environment scope per property
objective: Keep card data out of hotel systems where possible and protect the cardholder data environment where it remains.
requirement: Each property shall document its cardholder data environment, listing every terminal, POS station, server, network segment and person that stores, processes or transmits card data or can affect its security. The scope shall be confirmed at least yearly and after change.
rationale: Scope is assumed to cover front desk workstations, PMS server and POS network (A09), yet no property had written it down.
evidence_expected: CDE scope diagram;yearly scope confirmation record
assessment_question: Is there a current CDE scope document for the property confirmed in the last year?

title: Network separation of POS and payment terminals
objective: Keep card data out of hotel systems where possible and protect the cardholder data environment where it remains.
requirement: POS stations, payment terminals and their servers shall sit on a segment separated from guest Wi-Fi, back office, in room and engineering networks, with only documented flows allowed and the separation tested at least yearly.
rationale: The case network is likely flat (E12, A08), so any foothold could reach payment systems.
evidence_expected: segmentation diagram with firewall rules;segmentation test report
assessment_question: Does a test from guest, back office and engineering segments confirm no path into the payment segment?

title: Payment terminal inspection
objective: Keep card data out of hotel systems where possible and protect the cardholder data environment where it remains.
requirement: Payment terminals at the front desk, outlets, spa and banqueting shall be listed with serial numbers and inspected for tampering or substitution on a set schedule, with night and banqueting terminals checked at each shift handover.
rationale: Terminals sit in public areas used around the clock; tamper inspection is a step in the PCI SSC small merchant guide (INT B2).
evidence_expected: terminal register with serial numbers;inspection logs
assessment_question: Are all terminals listed and do inspection logs show checks at the set frequency?

title: Acquirer, gateway and aggregator agreements
objective: Keep card data out of hotel systems where possible and protect the cardholder data environment where it remains.
requirement: Every acquirer, gateway, payment aggregator and tokenisation provider shall be engaged under a written agreement that states its PCI DSS responsibilities. The property shall confirm the provider's compliance status at least yearly.
rationale: PCI DSS reaches hotels through acquirer and aggregator contracts (IU A14, USE B1) and outsourcing payment does not remove the duty.
evidence_expected: signed agreements with responsibility matrix;provider attestation of compliance for the current year
assessment_question: Does every payment provider have a written agreement with PCI responsibilities and a current compliance attestation?

title: Card data retention limits
objective: Keep card data out of hotel systems where possible and protect the cardholder data environment where it remains.
requirement: Card data shall not be kept after authorisation except as tokens; card data captured on paper, email, fax or call recordings shall be destroyed once the transaction settles. Sensitive authentication data shall never be stored.
rationale: Folios, emails and fallback forms are where hotels keep card numbers by habit (A10); Indian rules cap merchant retention at settlement (IU A13).
evidence_expected: card data retention procedure;quarterly card data discovery results
assessment_question: Does a discovery scan of mail, shares and paper stores find no card data held beyond settlement?

title: PCI DSS validation evidence
objective: Keep card data out of hotel systems where possible and protect the cardholder data environment where it remains.
requirement: Each property or the group on its behalf shall hold current PCI DSS validation evidence of the type its acquirer requires (a self assessment questionnaire or a report on compliance). Any failed requirement shall be tracked to closure.
rationale: The case group handled cards through the acquirer without a visible validation record (A17).
evidence_expected: current SAQ or ROC with attestation;remediation tracker for failed requirements
assessment_question: Is current PCI DSS validation evidence on file and are failed items tracked to closure?

title: Guest network isolation
objective: Give guests connectivity and in room services without exposing hotel systems or other guests.
requirement: Guest Wi-Fi shall give internet only access with client isolation, carry no route to hotel systems and use management interfaces and credentials separate from the corporate network.
rationale: The NIST hotel design gives guests an internet only path (INT C5) and HTNG calls for per user and device separation on converged networks (INT F2).
evidence_expected: wireless controller configuration;isolation test record
assessment_question: Does a test from a guest device show no route to hotel systems and no reach to other guest devices?

title: Reservation linked guest access
objective: Give guests connectivity and in room services without exposing hotel systems or other guests.
requirement: Guest Wi-Fi access shall be issued against the reservation or room through the PMS or captive portal, expire at checkout and keep access logs for the period the applicable obligations require.
rationale: Reservation tied credentials appear in the NIST design (INT C5); guest internet platform gateways in the case suggest a portal already exists (E10).
evidence_expected: portal configuration showing PMS link and expiry;access log retention setting
assessment_question: Do guest credentials expire at checkout and are access logs kept for the required period?

title: In room entertainment servers
objective: Give guests connectivity and in room services without exposing hotel systems or other guests.
requirement: In room entertainment and service request servers shall run no cleartext services such as FTP, Telnet or unencrypted mail relay, be patched as Tier 3 systems and sit in their own segment reachable from guest devices only through defined services.
rationale: FTP and SMTP ran on two in room system hosts in the case (E08, A12).
evidence_expected: service scan of in room servers;segment rule set
assessment_question: Does a scan of in room servers show no cleartext services and only defined flows from guest devices?

title: Casting and IPTV device hardening
objective: Give guests connectivity and in room services without exposing hotel systems or other guests.
requirement: Casting, smart TV and IPTV devices shall have default passwords changed, remote management limited to the hotel management network and firmware kept on a supported version.
rationale: Hundreds of identical room devices with default settings give an attacker a large and rarely checked foothold.
evidence_expected: device inventory with firmware versions;configuration check record
assessment_question: Are room devices on supported firmware with default passwords changed and management restricted?

title: Guest device data wipe at checkout
objective: Give guests connectivity and in room services without exposing hotel systems or other guests.
requirement: Any in room device or service that stores guest accounts, casting pairings or streaming logins shall be cleared automatically at checkout and the clearing verified before the next arrival.
rationale: Guests sign into streaming accounts on room televisions and the next guest inherits them if nothing clears the device.
evidence_expected: checkout wipe configuration or log;housekeeping or system verification checklist
assessment_question: For a sample of rooms, was guest data cleared at checkout before the next arrival?

title: Lock server receives room number only
objective: Keep electronic locking systems trustworthy and free of guest personal data.
requirement: The lock system interface shall receive only the room number, stay dates and key type from the PMS and shall hold no guest name, contact or payment data.
rationale: In the NIST hotel design the door lock server receives only a room number (INT C5); the case lock system connects through the interface server (A11).
evidence_expected: interface specification or message capture;lock database field review
assessment_question: Does the lock database hold any guest name, contact or payment field?

title: Key encoder workstation hardening
objective: Keep electronic locking systems trustworthy and free of guest personal data.
requirement: Key encoder workstations shall run only the lock software and its prerequisites, use individual operator logons, follow the workstation hardening baseline and log every key issued with operator and time.
rationale: Encoders sit at the front desk and issue access to every room; a door lock system was among the scanned hosts (E10).
evidence_expected: encoder workstation build sheet;key issue audit report
assessment_question: Do encoder workstations use individual logons and does the key log show operator and time?

title: Mobile and online key security
objective: Keep electronic locking systems trustworthy and free of guest personal data.
requirement: Where mobile or online keys are used, keys shall be issued only to authenticated guests linked to the reservation, protected with current encryption and revoked at checkout or on request. The vendor solution shall be assessed against the HTNG door lock guidance.
rationale: HTNG door lock guidance covers mobile key and online lock end points (INT F1); mobile keys extend the lock system onto guest phones.
evidence_expected: vendor security statement assessed against HTNG guidance;key revocation test record
assessment_question: Are mobile keys revoked at checkout and has the vendor solution been assessed against the HTNG guidance?

title: Lock vendor access and audit trail
objective: Keep electronic locking systems trustworthy and free of guest personal data.
requirement: Lock vendor support shall use the approved remote access path. The lock audit trail of key issue, master key use and door openings shall be retained and reviewable for incident investigation.
rationale: Door investigations after guest complaints depend on the lock audit trail. Lock vendors usually support systems remotely.
evidence_expected: vendor access records for the lock system;audit trail export sample
assessment_question: Can the property export the lock audit trail for a past date and show vendor access went through the approved path?

title: Engineering asset inventory
objective: Bring building and engineering systems under the same security discipline as IT systems.
requirement: Engineering shall keep an inventory of building management, energy, lift, fire, water treatment and in room control devices with protocol, network location, firmware, OEM and support contact, held in the group asset register.
rationale: No engineering system appeared in any case file (E20) though the assumed estate is large (A13).
evidence_expected: engineering asset register;network discovery reconciliation
assessment_question: Does the asset register list engineering devices with protocol, firmware and OEM contact?

title: BMS and IoT segmentation
objective: Bring building and engineering systems under the same security discipline as IT systems.
requirement: Building management and IoT systems shall sit on segments separated from guest, corporate and payment networks, with only documented flows to named management stations.
rationale: A flat network lets a compromised controller reach Tier 1 systems (P4, A08); HTNG calls for separating IoT on converged hotel networks (INT F2).
evidence_expected: segmentation diagram;firewall rule review for engineering segments
assessment_question: Are engineering segments separated with only documented flows to named stations?

title: Default credential removal on engineering devices
objective: Bring building and engineering systems under the same security discipline as IT systems.
requirement: Default and shared passwords on controllers, panels, gateways and engineering software shall be changed at commissioning and stored in a vault. Devices that cannot change them shall be listed as exceptions with compensating isolation.
rationale: Default credentials over BACnet and Modbus are an assumed path to altered HVAC, lighting or alarms (P5, A14).
evidence_expected: credential change record per device;exception entries for devices that cannot change
assessment_question: Have default passwords been changed on all engineering devices or recorded as exceptions?

title: OEM access control
objective: Bring building and engineering systems under the same security discipline as IT systems.
requirement: OEM and maintenance contractors shall reach engineering systems only through the approved vendor access path with named accounts, never through modems, permanently installed remote tools or shared logons.
rationale: Vendor access with shared accounts and no session logs is the first assumed engineering path (P1, A14).
evidence_expected: vendor access logs for engineering systems;review of remote tools installed on engineering stations
assessment_question: Does all OEM access to engineering systems go through the approved path with named accounts?

title: Protocol exposure and engineering workstation review
objective: Bring building and engineering systems under the same security discipline as IT systems.
requirement: Engineering shall review at least yearly which BACnet, Modbus and other building protocols are reachable from each segment and block them from guest and corporate networks. Engineering workstations shall keep drawings, camera layouts and contracts on access controlled shares with removable media scanned.
rationale: Building protocols often lack built in protection (Capstone 1 Section 2.3) and engineering shares and USB use are assumed paths P2 and P3 (A14).
evidence_expected: protocol exposure scan with remediation record;share permission review for engineering workstations
assessment_question: Was a protocol exposure review done this year and are engineering documents on access controlled shares?

title: Camera and recorder network separation
objective: Operate CCTV lawfully and protect footage as personal data.
requirement: IP cameras and recorders shall sit on a dedicated segment with no internet access except approved updates, have default credentials changed and be managed only from named stations.
rationale: CCTV is modelled on the engineering estate with no visible separation (A13).
evidence_expected: camera network diagram;recorder configuration export
assessment_question: Are cameras and recorders on their own segment with default credentials changed?

title: Footage retention and access
objective: Operate CCTV lawfully and protect footage as personal data.
requirement: Footage shall be kept only for a documented period set per camera purpose and jurisdiction, overwritten automatically after it and viewed only by named security roles.
rationale: Retention longer than needed is an assumed leakage point (A15) and EDPB guidance expects short retention for video (USE A2).
evidence_expected: retention configuration per recorder;access list for footage viewing
assessment_question: Does each recorder overwrite at the documented period and is viewing limited to named roles?

title: Footage export logging
objective: Operate CCTV lawfully and protect footage as personal data.
requirement: Every export of footage shall be authorised by a named manager, logged with requester, purpose and recipient, encrypted in transit and on media and tracked until returned or destroyed.
rationale: CCTV exports are an assumed leakage point across all stages (A15); police and insurer requests often arrive outside office hours.
evidence_expected: footage export register;record of encrypted export media
assessment_question: Is every footage export in the last quarter logged with an approver and encrypted?

title: CCTV signage and placement
objective: Operate CCTV lawfully and protect footage as personal data.
requirement: Monitored areas shall carry signage at eye level before entry with a route to a fuller privacy notice. Cameras shall never cover guest rooms, washrooms, changing rooms or other private areas.
rationale: EDPB guidance sets layered signage and excludes private areas (USE A2); recording people without consent is an offence in the UAE (IU B6).
evidence_expected: signage photographs per camera zone;camera placement plan
assessment_question: Does every monitored zone have eye level signage and does the placement plan exclude private areas?

title: One approved remote access path
objective: Allow vendor support only through one controlled, attributable and recorded path.
requirement: All vendor and staff remote access shall pass through one approved gateway per group or property that enforces MFA, encryption and logging; RDP, VNC and similar services shall not be reachable from the internet and internal RDP shall require network level authentication.
rationale: A remote support tool on 7 systems, VNC on 3, RDP on 13 with 4 lacking NLA and an SSH host reachable from the internet (E09).
evidence_expected: remote access architecture diagram;external exposure scan
assessment_question: Does an external scan show no remote service other than the approved gateway?

title: Named vendor accounts
objective: Allow vendor support only through one controlled, attributable and recorded path.
requirement: Each vendor engineer shall have a named account tied to a signed access agreement; shared vendor logons shall not be used and accounts shall be disabled when the contract or engineer changes.
rationale: Shared vendor accounts make it impossible to tell which engineer changed a system (P1, A14).
evidence_expected: vendor account register;signed vendor access agreements
assessment_question: Is every vendor account named, linked to an agreement and disabled for engineers who have left?

title: Time windowed vendor access with approval
objective: Allow vendor support only through one controlled, attributable and recorded path.
requirement: Vendor accounts shall stay disabled by default and be enabled for a set window only after approval by the system owner at the property, with out of hours emergencies approved by the duty manager and entered in the exception register.
rationale: Urgent vendor fixes during service hours are where operations most often bypass IT rules (E17).
evidence_expected: access request and approval tickets;account enablement log
assessment_question: Were all vendor sessions in the last month opened against an approved request?

title: Vendor session logging
objective: Allow vendor support only through one controlled, attributable and recorded path.
requirement: Vendor remote sessions to PMS, POS, lock, BMS and CCTV systems shall be logged with user, time and system. Sessions shall be recorded where the gateway supports it and recordings kept for at least 90 days.
rationale: Unlogged vendor changes to building systems are an assumed path (P1, A14) and no session logs were found (E20).
evidence_expected: session log sample;recording retention setting
assessment_question: Can the property produce a log or recording for a vendor session from last month?

title: Removal of unapproved remote tools
objective: Allow vendor support only through one controlled, attributable and recorded path.
requirement: Unapproved remote tools such as the remote support tool or VNC installs left by past vendors shall be removed from all systems. Software inventory scans shall flag any reinstallation.
rationale: Removing the vulnerable remote support tool client is one of the six Capstone 1 immediate fixes (E09).
evidence_expected: software inventory report showing removal;quarterly reinstallation check
assessment_question: Does the latest software inventory show no unapproved remote tool on any system?

title: Guest data map from booking to archive
objective: Handle guest data lawfully and minimally from booking to deletion.
requirement: [GROUP] shall maintain a guest data map covering booking, PMS, registration, billing, CRM and loyalty, backup and archive that lists data types, systems, processors, transfers and known leakage points such as shared folders, USB media, printed folios and email attachments.
rationale: The Capstone 1 lifecycle found nine assumed leakage points across six stages (A15) and no classification scheme (E20).
evidence_expected: guest data map with data flow diagram;yearly review record
assessment_question: Is there a current guest data map naming systems, processors and leakage points for each stage?

title: Identity document capture and masking
objective: Handle guest data lawfully and minimally from booking to deletion.
requirement: Passport and identity document images shall be captured only where law or a stated purpose requires, stored in one controlled location linked to the stay, masked on screens and printouts where the full number is not needed and encrypted at rest.
rationale: ID scans are collected at registration (A10) and regulators cited unencrypted passport numbers in hotel breach cases (USE A13, B8).
evidence_expected: ID capture procedure;storage and screen configuration showing masking and encryption
assessment_question: Are ID images stored in one encrypted location and masked where the full number is not needed?

title: Legal guest register duties
objective: Handle guest data lawfully and minimally from booking to deletion.
requirement: Each property shall meet the guest registration duty of its jurisdiction, such as Form III submission within 24 hours of arrival and of departure in India or the traveller registers of Germany and Spain, through an integrated and access controlled process with submission evidence kept for the required period.
rationale: Guest registers are legal duties with short clocks and their data is highly sensitive (IU A10, USE A8, USE A10).
evidence_expected: register submission log;access list for the register system
assessment_question: Were all foreign guest register submissions made within the legal clock last month?

title: Retention and deletion schedule
objective: Handle guest data lawfully and minimally from booking to deletion.
requirement: A retention schedule shall set a period for each guest data type based on legal duties and purpose. Data past its period shall be deleted or anonymised in the PMS, CRM, email, shared drives, backups and paper archives on a set cycle.
rationale: Retention longer than needed is assumed in the absence of a policy (A10, L8) and regulators have ordered written retention policies for hotel loyalty data (USE B8).
evidence_expected: retention schedule;deletion job log or destruction certificates
assessment_question: Was the deletion cycle run on schedule across every listed store?

title: Guest rights handling
objective: Handle guest data lawfully and minimally from booking to deletion.
requirement: Guest requests to access, correct, delete or opt out shall be logged, verified and answered within the shortest applicable legal period, no more than 90 days for India, using one process across properties and brands.
rationale: Indian rules set a 90 day maximum (IU A3) and US and EU rules add their own rights; one process avoids per property improvisation.
evidence_expected: request log with response times;identity verification procedure
assessment_question: Were all guest rights requests in the last year answered within the legal period?

title: Minimisation in loyalty and marketing
objective: Handle guest data lawfully and minimally from booking to deletion.
requirement: Loyalty and marketing systems shall collect only the fields needed for the programme, record the basis or consent for marketing, honour opt outs in every channel and keep children's data out of profiling.
rationale: Loyalty data has been central in hotel enforcement cases (USE B8, B14) and the case deck cites a loyalty app breach (E19).
evidence_expected: loyalty data field list with purposes;consent and opt out records
assessment_question: Does each loyalty field have a stated purpose and are opt outs honoured in all channels?

title: SaaS and cloud register
objective: Know every cloud service holding hotel data and the security duties the hotel keeps for each.
requirement: [GROUP] shall keep a register of every cloud and SaaS service holding hotel or guest data, such as booking engine, channel manager, CRM, email and cloud backup, with owner, data types, data location, contract and exit plan.
rationale: Booking engine, channel manager, CRM, email and backup storage are assumed to be SaaS (A06) yet were not listed anywhere.
evidence_expected: SaaS register;reconciliation with finance or single sign on records
assessment_question: Does the register list every cloud service found in finance or sign on records?

title: Shared responsibility matrix per service
objective: Know every cloud service holding hotel data and the security duties the hotel keeps for each.
requirement: For each cloud service a shared responsibility matrix shall record which security tasks sit with the provider and which stay with the hotel, including users, access, endpoints, data classification and configuration.
rationale: Provider models keep identities, data and endpoints with the customer in every service model (INT E3, E4).
evidence_expected: completed responsibility matrix per service;review sign off
assessment_question: Does each cloud service holding guest data have a signed responsibility matrix?

title: Provider assurance
objective: Know every cloud service holding hotel data and the security duties the hotel keeps for each.
requirement: Each provider holding guest or payment data shall supply current assurance before contract and every year after, such as a CSA STAR entry, an ISO/IEC 27001 certificate or a SOC 2 report. Gaps shall be recorded as risks.
rationale: STAR levels pair the CAIQ with ISO/IEC 27001 or SOC 2 (INT E2) and give a hotel buyer a checkable filter.
evidence_expected: provider assurance file;risk entries for assurance gaps
assessment_question: Does every provider holding guest or payment data have current assurance on file?

title: Cloud administrator protection
objective: Know every cloud service holding hotel data and the security duties the hotel keeps for each.
requirement: Administrator and privileged accounts for every cloud console and SaaS service shall be named and use MFA and single sign on where offered. Break glass accounts shall be sealed, tested and alerted on use.
rationale: The customer always keeps accounts and access management in SaaS (INT E4) and a lost console password exposes every property at once.
evidence_expected: single sign on and MFA configuration exports;break glass test record
assessment_question: Do all cloud administrators use named MFA accounts and was break glass access tested?

title: Data location and transfer check
objective: Know every cloud service holding hotel data and the security duties the hotel keeps for each.
requirement: Before guest or payment data is placed with a provider, [GROUP] shall confirm where it is stored and processed and that a lawful transfer basis exists for each jurisdiction, such as adequacy or contract clauses for EU data and transfer conditions under the UAE PDPL.
rationale: Transfer rules differ in the EU, the UAE and India (USE A1, IU B1) and SaaS providers often process data in several regions.
evidence_expected: data location statement from the provider;transfer assessment record
assessment_question: Is a data location statement and transfer assessment on file for every provider holding guest data?

title: Supplier security clauses
objective: Carry security requirements through supplier, franchise and management agreements and acquisitions.
requirement: Contracts with suppliers that access hotel systems or guest data shall include security, confidentiality, breach notice, audit, sub processor and return or deletion clauses scaled to the risk of the service.
rationale: No vendor contracts were available in the case files (E20) and several laws require processor contracts (USE A1, B5).
evidence_expected: contract clause library;sample of signed contracts containing the clauses
assessment_question: Do sampled supplier contracts contain the required security clauses?

title: Critical vendor risk review
objective: Carry security requirements through supplier, franchise and management agreements and acquisitions.
requirement: Vendors whose failure or compromise would stop guest service or expose guest data, such as PMS, payment, lock, Wi-Fi and BMS vendors, shall be risk reviewed at onboarding and at least yearly with results fed into the risk register.
rationale: Hotels depend on a few vendors for every core system (A16) and a state settlement required risk assessments of critical IT vendors (USE B14).
evidence_expected: critical vendor list;completed vendor review records
assessment_question: Was every critical vendor reviewed in the last year?

title: Security schedule in franchise and management agreements
objective: Carry security requirements through supplier, franchise and management agreements and acquisitions.
requirement: Each franchise or hotel management agreement shall carry a security schedule that assigns HISS controls to brand, operator, owner or franchisee, treats franchisee networks as untrusted from the brand side and sets assessment and reporting duties.
rationale: A federal order against a hotel franchisor required franchisee networks to be treated as untrusted (USE B7).
evidence_expected: signed security schedule;responsibility matrix per agreement
assessment_question: Does every franchise or management agreement carry a security schedule with a responsibility matrix?

title: Brand and operator audit alignment
objective: Carry security requirements through supplier, franchise and management agreements and acquisitions.
requirement: Brand, operator and owner security audits shall be mapped to HISS controls so that one evidence set answers all of them. Findings from any audit shall enter the single remediation tracker of the property.
rationale: In the student's experience audits treated security as a side topic with undefined controls (E17) and properties answer several audit formats (A17).
evidence_expected: audit to HISS mapping;consolidated remediation tracker
assessment_question: Are all audit findings for the property held in one tracker mapped to HISS controls?

title: Acquisition and onboarding assessment
objective: Carry security requirements through supplier, franchise and management agreements and acquisitions.
requirement: Before a property joins [GROUP] by acquisition, conversion or new management contract its systems shall be assessed against HISS. Within 90 days of joining it shall be scanned and connected to group monitoring or kept isolated until it is.
rationale: Regulators held a hotel group liable for breaches in systems it acquired and required assessments on acquisition (USE A13, B14).
evidence_expected: pre acquisition assessment report;90 day integration checklist
assessment_question: Was the last property to join assessed beforehand and integrated or isolated within 90 days?
